q: Is unpaid leave taken out of my pay on working days or on calendar days?
log:
Based on this document, I have the answer.

Unpaid leave is deducted from your pay on a **calendar-day basis, not working days**. Specifically:

- Basic pay and nontaxable allowances (meal, own-car, etc.) are prorated using the ratio **days worked ÷ calendar days in the month**.
- This uses the full calendar days in the month, not just working days — the same basis used when someone joins or leaves mid-month.
- Example: a 5-day unpaid stretch inside a 31-day month removes 5/31 of pay and allowances, regardless of how many of those 5 days would have been working days.
- Insurance deduction lines fall automatically as a consequence, since they're based on pay excluding nontaxable allowances.

So: **calendar days**, not working days.

DONE
